entries.title: Greatest common divisor: trial divisors vs Euclid's algorithm

algorithms.name: trial divisors
algorithms.time_complexity: Theta(2^n) iterations in the worst case: exactly min(a, b) - gcd(a, b) + 1 iterations of one or two divisions, i.e. up to 2^n - 2 on coprime n-bit inputs (>= 2^(n-2) on the coprime Fibonacci pairs used for V2). In bit operations, Theta(2^n) times the cost of an n-bit division.

algorithms.name: Euclid's algorithm
algorithms.time_complexity: O(n) division steps: at most log_phi(min(a, b)) + O(1) <= 1.44 n + O(1) (Lame 1844), attained by consecutive Fibonacci numbers. O(n^2) bit operations with schoolbook division: a step with quotient q on numbers of at most n bits costs O(n (1 + log q)), and the log q sum to at most n; Theta(n^2) on consecutive Fibonacci numbers, where each of the Theta(n) steps divides Theta(n)-bit numbers.

entries.title: Modular exponentiation: repeated multiplication vs square-and-multiply

lower_bounds.bound: at least ceil(log2 e) >= n - 1 multiplications (each multiplication at most doubles the largest exponent computed so far)
lower_bounds.setting: addition-chain (multiplication-only) model: each step multiplies two powers of a computed earlier

algorithms.name: repeated multiplication
algorithms.time_complexity: Theta(e) = Theta(2^n) multiplications mod m (exactly e of them, and e >= 2^(n-1))

algorithms.name: left-to-right square-and-multiply (binary method)

entries.title: Comparison sorting: insertion sort vs merge sort

lower_bounds.bound: Omega(n log n) comparisons: at least log2(n!) = n log2 n - O(n) in the worst case, and also on average over a uniformly random input order, hence in expectation for any randomized comparison sort
lower_bounds.setting: comparison model (elements are accessed only through pairwise comparisons)
lower_bounds.source: Knuth TAOCP Vol. 3 (1998), 5.3.1 (decision-tree argument, worst and average case); the randomized case follows from the average case by Yao's minimax principle

algorithms.name: insertion sort
algorithms.time_complexity: Theta(n + I) where I is the number of inversions: Theta(n^2) in the worst case (reversed input, I = n(n-1)/2) and on average over uniformly random inputs (E[I] ~ n^2/4, the case measured for V2); Theta(n) on sorted input

algorithms.name: merge sort
algorithms.time_complexity: Theta(n log n) on every input: T(n) = 2 T(n/2) + Theta(n)

entries.title: Exact string matching: naive scan vs Knuth-Morris-Pratt

algorithms.name: naive matching
algorithms.time_complexity: Theta(n m) character comparisons in the worst case (at most (n - m + 1) m, attained e.g. by T = a^n, P = a^(m-1) b); Theta(n^2) for the m = n // 2 instances used in V2

algorithms.name: Knuth-Morris-Pratt
algorithms.time_complexity: Theta(n + m) on every input: at most 2n comparisons in the scan and 2m to build the failure table (amortised: each comparison either advances the text position or shrinks the matched length); Theta(n) when m = Theta(n)

entries.title: Simon's problem: Theta(2^(n/2)) classical queries vs O(n) quantum queries

algorithms.name: classical collision search
algorithms.time_complexity: Theta(2^(n/2)) queries expected (birthday bound)

algorithms.name: Simon's quantum algorithm
